title: TP: add per-rank heartbeat metrics, stall reason codes, and structured stall logs
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes:
- Adds TP heartbeat + in-flight collective metrics to improve stall detection/diagnostics.
- Adds stall_reason codes and structured logs on suspected TP stalls.
- No API behavior changes; metrics are low-cardinality and gated by config where appropriate.
body: Context: Under sustained TP load we’ve seen “silent stalls” where requests hang (often streaming decode) but the only visible symptom is downstream timeouts and eventual replica churn. This PR adds low-cardinality TP liveness + progress metrics and a standardized stall reason taxonomy so SRE/on-call can quickly answer: is it compute, comms/NCCL, or scheduler starvation? Scope in this PR is instrumentation only (no scheduling/comms correctness changes). Related: ENG-4823 (instrumentation), ENG-4821 (initiative umbrella). What’s included: (1) Per-rank heartbeat metrics: a monotonic heartbeat updated at key progress points (prefill start/end, decode step start/end, before/after collective calls). Exported as both a counter and “seconds since last heartbeat” gauge so alerting is straightforward. (2) In-flight collective counters: increments/decrements around NCCL collectives and exposes last seen collective sequence per TP group to help identify mismatched ordering vs global stalls. (3) Stall reason codes: introduces a shared enum used by scheduler/runtime to tag suspected stall sites (compute, comms collective, scheduler starvation/backpressure, kv cache compaction, cancellation path, unknown). This is deliberately small + stable; we can extend later but want to avoid high churn and label cardinality explosions. (4) Structured logs on stall suspicion: when heartbeat gaps exceed a threshold (see below) or when a step crosses the “soft stall” deadline, we emit a single structured log entry with enough context to correlate across ranks. (5) Unit tests: fake-clock tests validate heartbeat progression, ensure we do not emit high-frequency logs under normal operation, and verify reason codes map to expected metric labels. Metric names (agreed w/ SRE in Slack thread 1739897721): - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_total{model,cluster,replica,tp_rank,tp_world_size,phase} - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds{model,cluster,replica,tp_rank,tp_world_size} - redwood_runtime_tp_inflight_collectives{collective,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} - redwood_runtime_tp_last_collective_seq{collective,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} - redwood_runtime_tp_stall_suspected_total{reason,model,cluster,replica,tp_group_id} Stall reason taxonomy (initial): - STALL_REASON_UNSPECIFIED - STALL_REASON_COMPUTE (kernel/compute step didn’t advance) - STALL_REASON_NCCL_COLLECTIVE (in-flight collective didn’t complete) - STALL_REASON_SCHEDULER_STARVATION (no scheduling progress / queue fairness) - STALL_REASON_KV_COMPACTION (compaction/eviction path blocking) - STALL_REASON_CANCELLATION_PATH (client disconnect / cancellation leaving ranks waiting) - STALL_REASON_UNKNOWN Structured log fields (sample): event=tp_stall_suspected request_id=<uuid> replica_id=<id> model=<name> tp_group_id=<id> tp_world_size=<n> tp_rank=<r> phase=<prefill|decode> stall_reason=<enum> heartbeat_age_ms=<ms> inflight_collectives=<n> last_collective_seq=<seq> scheduler_queue_depth=<n> stream_id=<cuda stream int> note=<short> Config/overhead notes: - Heartbeat updates are intentionally lightweight (atomic + timestamp). We avoid per-request labels; replica_id/model are already present in our standard metric dimensions. - redwood_runtime_tp_rank_heartbeat_age_seconds is updated once per scrape (computed from last heartbeat timestamp) and does not require timers per request. - Structured stall logs are rate limited per (replica,tp_group_id,reason) to 1/min by default to avoid log storms during incident conditions. - A “soft suspicion” threshold is currently 5s heartbeat age; this is not paging by itself. Alert rules/paging thresholds will be implemented in observability-pack PR-412 after we get a few days of baseline. Dashboards: - Draft panels are referenced here (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/tp-stalls/tp-stall-and-timeout (WIP; final panels/alerts tracked in observability-pack PR-412) - Confluence dashboard doc: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tp-stall-and-timeout-dashboard.json (linked in ENG-4823) Validation: - benchmark-lab mixed workload repro: heartbeat progresses under normal load; when forced to block a mocked collective, inflight_collectives stays >0 and heartbeat_age_seconds increases and emits a single structured stall log per minute. - Local tests: runtime_unit_tests pass; added coverage for stall reason mapping + rate limiter. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add trace span attributes for collective counters/rank IDs (tracked in PR-21872). - Wire in scheduler queue depth (we included a placeholder hook; scheduler team will fill real signal in ENG-4824/PR-21841). - Alert rules + paging policy (observability-pack PR-412 + SRE thread 1740071202).
commits: runtime/metrics: add TP heartbeat counters + heartbeat age gauge
runtime/tp: introduce TpStallReason enum + mapping helpers
runtime/logging: structured tp_stall_suspected event + rate limiter
runtime/nccl: add in-flight collective counters + last collective seq
tests: fake-clock unit tests for heartbeat progression + log rate limiting
docs: add metric definitions + dashboard link to runtime ops notes
changed_files_high_level: runtime/tests/test_tp_heartbeat.cc (new): fake clock + rate limit tests
conversation: Julian Moore (review): Can we confirm we’re not adding request_id / prompt_id as metric labels anywhere? We can’t afford cardinality spikes during incidents. Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed. request_id only in structured logs (rate limited). Metrics labels are restricted to the standard runtime dimensions (model/cluster/replica + tp_rank/world_size/group_id + reason/phase/collective). Aisha Bello (review): Naming looks good. For alerting, I’d prefer a gauge like “heartbeat age seconds” rather than having to do PromQL math off a counter. Looks like you added that — thanks. Can you add a note on scrape-time computation to avoid per-request timers? Omar El-Sayed (author): Added to PR description + docs: heartbeat_age_seconds computed from last_heartbeat_ns and exported at scrape. Allison Grant (review): Please align stall reason strings with trace attribute naming conventions (snake_case). Right now the log emits “STALL_REASON_NCCL_COLLECTIVE”; could we also emit a lowercase variant for easier querying? Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated log schema to emit stall_reason="nccl_collective" while keeping enum constant internally; added unit test for mapping stability. Noah Patel (review): +1. Minor: the “soft suspicion threshold” default (5s) seems aggressive for long-context prefill. Can we make it phase-aware or just call it “debug threshold” for now? Omar El-Sayed (author): Renamed to “soft suspicion threshold (debug)” and made it configurable per phase with conservative defaults: prefill=15s, decode=5s. Default values are intentionally non-paging; SRE will tune alerting separately. Sofia Ivanova (review): Good. I’d like to ensure scheduler starvation reason is not used until scheduler actually sets it; otherwise it’ll bias incidents. Omar El-Sayed (author): Agreed—by default we emit UNKNOWN unless explicit reason is set by caller. Added comment + guard in the helper. Approvals: Julian Moore (APPROVED), Aisha Bello (APPROVED), Allison Grant (APPROVED), Noah Patel (APPROVED).
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-4824 (scheduler fixes), PR-21872 (trace attributes), and observability-pack PR-412 (dashboards/alerts).
